newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: New owners take over MRC Allied from Osmena.
newsitem.headline: New owners take over MRC Allied from Osmena.

text.p: Real estate development firm MRC Allied Industries Inc said on Tuesday businessmen Benjamin Bitanga and Augusto Syjuco have taken over management control from EMRO Holdings Inc.
EMRO Holdings Inc, owned by presidential adviser for economic affairs Emilio Osmena, had sold 80 million shares to Bitanga and his partner Syjuco, a statement issued by the company said.
It, however, did not disclose the purchase price.
"The purchase represents 16 percent of the company's outstanding shares of stock previously held by EMRO Holdings.
Together with their old holdings, the new group now owns 45 percent of MRC Allied," the statement said.
EMRO used to own 37.6 percent of the company, while Bitanga, 28.8 percent. It sold 33.6 percent of its shares to the public in 1995.
Bitanga has interests in real estate development, while Syjuco, a prominent businessman in southern Philippines, is into financial services.
Syjuco said he decided to invest in MRC after studying the potential of its industrial estate projects in the central Cebu and Leyte provinces.

"It is a major shift for us to go into real estate development, but considering that we are now building up our financial and banking businesses in the south and MRC is concentrating in the south as well, we thought the synergies are there, and one reinforces the other," he said.
MRC Allied closed five centavos lower at 3.35 pesos on Tuesday. - Manila newsroom 63 2 8418938 Fax 8176267
